summary: For every 0<epsilon<=1/2, iid cap-one uniforms give Q=2epsilon X1X2+2X1X3+2X2X4+2epsilon^{-1}X3X4=2(X1+X4/epsilon)(epsilon X2+X3), whose density has a logarithmic singularity although the physical pair (1,2) has zero diagonals, mutual edge epsilon arbitrarily small, the outside slope pair (X3,X4) has joint density cap one, and the transverse 2x2 slope minor equals one. The matrix has only two nonzero eigenvalues +/- (epsilon+epsilon^{-1}), so this is not a QFORM counterexample. It refutes perturbative extension of the exact-zero-pair two-slope L-infinity theorem using only the same slope-cap/minor currency; a genuine third spectral/product-preserving resource must be spent before the aligned rank-two product singularity forms.
